paper_metadata.title: Q-DTN: A Quantum-Enhanced Framework for Secure Financial Risk Management

experiments.description: Quantum-Enhanced Risk Classifier (QERC) evaluated for financial fraud/risk detection using a hybrid QSVM-VQC pipeline on public financial datasets, with performance reported under 5-fold cross-validation.

algorithm.variant: Quantum-Enhanced Risk Classifier (QERC) combining QSVM and VQC
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Convergence typically achieved within 50 iterations; pseudocode sets maximum iterations Tmax = 100 and stops when |Lt-1 - Lt| < ϵ

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical financial data x is amplitude-encoded into a quantum state |ϕ(x)⟩; paper states only 5 qubits are required for 23-dimensional FICO data and n = ceil(log2(d)) qubits for d-dimensional input
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_θ L(θ) = (1/N) Σ_i ℓ(y_i, <ψ(x_i, θ)| O |ψ(x_i, θ)>) with hinge loss ℓ(y, f) = max(0, 1 - y·f)

problem_instance.description: Financial fraud/risk classification on multiple public datasets including credit scoring and DeFi fraud detection
problem_instance.dataset_name: FICO HELOC; Ethereum transaction logs; IoT climate finance data

dataset_specification.description: FICO HELOC: 10,459 credit profiles, 23 features. Ethereum transaction logs: 100,000 DeFi transactions. IoT climate finance: 9,356 records, 12 features. Data normalized to [0,1] with differential privacy ε = 0.1. Evaluation reported with 5-fold cross-validation.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Preprocessing and anonymization off-chain; data normalized to [0,1]; differential privacy (ε = 0.1) applied for anonymization; amplitude encoding used for quantum input
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 5-fold cross-validation; paired t-test with Bonferroni correction; scalability tests on 1,000 to 1,000,000 samples

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data preprocessing and anonymization off-chain; normalization to [0,1]; differential privacy ε = 0.1
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of Pauli-Z expectation values; sign-based prediction; SHAP-based explanation module used separately for interpretability

speedup_claims.conditions: training time comparison on public financial datasets under 5-fold cross-validation
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as 10 s vs 500 s for XGBoost and 600 s for neural networks; simulation-based on IBM Qiskit Aer, not hardware deployment.

speedup_claims.factor: O(log2 d) qubits / O(log N) feature-space dimensionality
speedup_claims.conditions: for d-dimensional input data and high-dimensional feature mapping
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper frames this as a complexity advantage; practical speedups depend on NISQ limitations and encoding constraints.

speedup_claims.conditions: stated in abstract as a summary claim
speedup_claims.caveats: No detailed overhead metric or calculation is provided in the body text.
Presented in related-work/background discussion and algorithm description; not tied to a separate controlled benchmark table.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log N) feature space dimensionality; O(log2 d) qubits for d-dimensional input
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: 500 s for XGBoost; 600 s for neural networks

experiments.description: Explainable Quantum AI (XQAI) module evaluating SHAP-style feature attribution over QERC quantum outputs for fraud/risk explanation.

algorithm.variant: XQAI adapting SHAP to quantum outputs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Feature subsets are evaluated by perturbing amplitude-encoded quantum states and sampling circuit expectation values
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute feature importance / SHAP values for QERC predictions

problem_instance.description: Interpretation of QERC fraud/risk predictions on the same financial datasets used by Q-DTN
problem_instance.dataset_name: FICO HELOC; Ethereum transaction logs; IoT climate finance data

dataset_specification.description: Uses the same datasets as the main QERC experiment; feature importance reported with transaction amount identified as primary predictor in DeFi fraud case study

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Perturbations applied to amplitude-encoded states; SHAP values estimated from sampled expectation values on IBM Qiskit Aer simulator
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Qualitative/interpretive evaluation; no separate quantitative benchmark reported

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: SHAP aggregation and visualization via heatmaps and decision trees

experiments.description: Decentralized Trust Network (DTN) evaluation for secure storage and sharing of risk data using Hyperledger Fabric smart contracts and zk-SNARK verification.

algorithm.variant: Blockchain-based Decentralized Trust Network with smart contracts and zk-SNARKs

hyperparameters.storage_model: off-chain sensitive data with on-chain hashes

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Risk data are stored as hashes on-chain; sensitive data remain off-chain; smart contract stores timestamped records and verifies zk-SNARK proofs
problem_formulation.objective_function: Secure, auditable risk data storage and sharing
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Authorization checks and zk-SNARK proof verification before storage/sharing

problem_instance.description: Secure sharing of financial risk data among participating institutions

dataset_specification.description: Smart contract operates on risk data identifiers, hashes, recipient node IDs, and zk proofs; no explicit dataset split reported

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Sensitive data stored off-chain; on-chain hash storage; audit trail logging
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: System-level simulation on a 10-node Hyperledger Fabric network; transaction throughput and latency mentioned as metrics, but no numeric results reported

hardware.device_name: Hyperledger Fabric network on AWS EC2

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Off-chain preprocessing and anonymization; hash generation; zk-SNARK proof generation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Audit logging, event emission, and retrieval of stored records
